title: You stay accountable
point: The assistant drafts and you decide: you own everything you send, sign or act on, whoever wrote the first version.
definition: Accountability means you answer for the result of your work. Using an AI assistant does not transfer that responsibility to the tool or its supplier.

objective.text: Given three AI-assisted work situations, identify who is accountable, list when AI use must be disclosed, and choose when to escalate to a manager or specialist.

misconceptions.claim: If the AI made the mistake, it is not my fault.
misconceptions.correction: Your name is on the email, report or decision. Customers, managers and regulators hold the sender responsible, not the software.

misconceptions.claim: Disclosing AI use makes my work look less professional.
misconceptions.correction: Where policy or the client requires disclosure, hiding it breaks trust and may break rules. Disclosure shows you used a tool responsibly and checked the result.

l1: You own what you send. Read every AI draft in full before it leaves your hands.
Disclose AI use where your policy, your client or the situation requires it.
Escalate when the stakes are high, such as legal exposure, large sums, safety or decisions about a person.
The assistant drafts, you decide. It never has the final word.
l2: Aisha in legal operations uses an assistant to draft a reply to a supplier dispute. The draft concedes a point the company has not agreed.
Because the reply has legal consequences, she does not send it. She passes the draft to the contracts lawyer and notes that AI produced the first version.
The lawyer corrects the concession, and Aisha sends the approved text under her own name.
l3: A reasonable escalation rule uses a threshold. For example, escalate any AI-drafted message that commits the company to more than a set sum or a legal position.
If a team sends 200 AI-assisted messages a month and 5 cross the threshold, escalation adds review time to only 2.5 per cent of them.
That small cost protects against the few messages where one mistake could cost far more than the time saved.
